reason: This Genesis 27 narrative actually demonstrates people actively expressing their views. Jacob expresses his concerns about the deception to his mother (v. 11-12), Rebekah speaks her plans clearly, Isaac communicates his wishes to both sons, and notably, Esau expresses his distress with a great and bitter cry (v. 34) and appeals to his father for blessing. While Rebekah does command Jacob to obey without further question ('let your curse be on me, my son; just obey my voice'), the passage overall shows multiple instances of people speaking, being heard, and responding to one another's expressions. The text depicts family dialogue and response to stated views rather than systematic discouragement of expression.
